/-!
# Erdős Problem 412

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/412](https://www.erdosproblems.com/412)

Reviewed by @b-mehta on 2025-05-27
-/

@[expose] public section

open ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos412

/--
Let $σ_1(n)=σ(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $σ_k(n) = σ(σ_{k-1}(n))$.
Is it true that, for every $m, n ≥ 2$, there exist some $i, j$ such that $σ_i(m) = σ_j(n)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_412 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (m ≥ 2) (n ≥ 2), ∃ i j, (σ 1)^[i] m = (σ 1)^[j] n := by
  sorry

end Erdos412

reformulations.difference: The source defines the iterated sequence starting at σ₁, while Lean allows iteration indices i,j : ℕ, including zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any equality f^[i](m) = f^[j](n) yields f^[i+1](m) = f^[j+1](n) by applying f to both sides, so every meeting has witnesses with both indices positive. The reverse implication simply forgets positivity. Thus allowing zero iterations does not change the conjecture.
